text:
maya: Quick perf note — after swapping to the fused-attn kernel we saw a 20-30% p99 tail increase specifically on tiny microbatches (<8 tokens). Suspect continuous batching window + jitter interaction is causing cache churn and frequent kernel handoffs.

leo: Can you paste the profiler snapshot and current window params?

maya: Pasting short extract from the run (canary):
```
run_id: canary-2026-03-17
micro_interval_ms: 2
coalesce_delay_ms: 1.2
jitter_ms: 0.6
token_budget_target: 64
kernel: fused-attn-v2
KV_cache_hit: 78%
P50: 12ms P95: 48ms P99: 210ms
context_switches: +18% vs baseline
kernel_swap_count: 1.9x
```

maya: Also saw momentary KV eviction spikes when coalesced batches formed with heterogeneous seq lengths — hot KV shards getting primed repeatedly. :thinking:

ashley: 78% hit isn't terrible but with kernel_swap_count that high it could explain p99. token_budget_target=64 feels aggressive for 2ms micro_interval — queues may force small batch flushes that prime new kernels.

ryan: Agreed. Two quick experiments to try: 1) increase jitter to 1.8ms to decorrelate arrivals 2) reduce token_budget_target to 32 for the tiny-window buckets. Both low-risk A/B.

leo: Also try sticky kernel affinity for a short period (e.g., keep requests pinned to same kernel instance if slot recently used) — avoids hot swap thrash. Could add a cheap LRU on kernels keyed by model+seqlen_bucket.

maya: I ran experiment A (jitter=1.8ms) on 5% traffic for 30m: p99 dropped from 210ms -> 145ms, KV_hit -> 83%, kernel_swap_count -> 1.2x. CPU scheduling variance still up but better.

maya: Experiment B (token_budget=32) on another 5% looked promising for small seqs: tail down to 130ms but throughput lowered ~3% overall.

ashley: Tradeoff is clear — smaller token budget reduces cross-seq batch heterogeneity and primes less KV, but you lose batching efficiency. For guests, maybe route tiny-seq requests to a separate low-latency path with lower budget.

ryan: If we combine jitter=1.8ms + token_budget=40 maybe hit a sweet spot. Can we run a 10% combi for 1h and capture kernel_swap_count, KV_hit, and cost delta?

maya: I'll spin that up. Quick note on profiling hooks: added a lightweight tag to samples to expose kernel_id and kv_shard_id in traces — helped confirm evictions line up with kernel swaps.

leo: Nice. After the combi run, let's also run a kernel-rollback canary (fused-attn-v1) to see absolute regression. We need solid A/B before any release decision. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: deploy-canary started for config "jitter-1.8_token-40_canary" on 10% traffic — ci/3821. Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/3821

maya: Thanks — will post results in ~75m. If numbers hold, propose default jitter bump to 1.2ms and a dynamic token_budget schedule (tiny_seq -> 32, small_seq -> 40, large_seq -> 64).

leo: Sounds good. Also open a quick RFC to capture kernel-affinity sticky policy and control flags for canary rollback.

maya: Filed RFC: runtime/2026-03-kernel-affinity.md — link in #eng-runtime when ready.

ryan: tl;dr: increase jitter, moderate token budget down-shift for tiny seq, consider sticky kernel short-term. Good work team. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
